answer: Recursive ZK reputation commitments anchor each node in a vault of staked collateral, so a Sybil clone must replay a gale of prior VRF transcripts that are information-theoretically bound to unique randomness. Zero-knowledge verifiable delay forces every new identity to traverse a dune of sequential proof work, while slashing penalties set negative expected attack utility below the rational threshold. Hence identity cloning is computationally infeasible and the protocol converges to a robust Nash equilibrium.
